problem: A scalar Linux RawUART write could accept physical bytes then fail during a later write/drain. Its early error return skipped WireDrain and Capacity accounting; a same-ID logical retry could bypass physical capacity already consumed. Mesh and bounded-pair paths already accounted accepted prefixes.

reproduction.transport: Actual nonblocking PTY with prefilled output and a supported4096B payload; no reader consumes during attempted write.

fix: Use the same existing counted polling loop for Linux scalar writes. Commit actual accepted prefix to accumulated virtual WireDrain and unchanged air/quiet accounting before returning original error. Only full successful write+drain earns ordinary bank credit or promotes a close. Zero-accepted failures retain old behavior.
